levels.required: A normative requirement. Mechanically proven violations fail strict conformance unless the rule explicitly allows an exception.
levels.recommended: A strong default. Deviations can be healthy when the project has a better local reason.
levels.advisory: A diagnostic or growth signal that should trigger review, not automatic restructuring.

rules.title: One canonical owner
rules.summary: Each class of durable information has one canonical owner; other surfaces link instead of maintaining independent copies.

rules.title: Separate information lifecycles
rules.summary: Current truth, active work, historical record, evidence, and enforcement remain distinguishable.

rules.title: Earn permanent structure
rules.summary: Create persistent files, directories, and workflows only after an observed responsibility justifies them.

rules.title: Persist expensive knowledge
rules.summary: Durable knowledge should primarily capture non-obvious information that is repeatedly useful or costly to rediscover.

rules.title: Promote through evidence
rules.summary: Information should begin at the narrowest useful scope and become durable or mechanical only when evidence justifies promotion.

rules.title: Retire obsolete structure
rules.summary: Delete, archive, demote, or supersede structures that no longer earn their maintenance cost.

rules.title: Keep persistent agent instructions scoped
rules.summary: Always-loaded instructions should contain broad non-derivable rules and routing cues, not active task state or repository encyclopedias.

rules.title: Avoid unmanaged instruction copies
rules.summary: Multiple tool-specific instruction files should have explicit independent scope or be generated, linked, or checked for drift.

rules.title: Separate information from authority
rules.summary: Plans, handoffs, status, and history do not grant controlled action authority unless the project explicitly defines an authorization mechanism and scope.

rules.title: Graduate repeatable hard rules to enforcement
rules.summary: Repeated mechanically checkable correctness or safety rules should move toward tests, schemas, hooks, permissions, or CI.

rules.title: README owns introduction and normal usage
rules.summary: README should not become an active handoff, work log, blocker list, or release diary.

rules.title: Changelog owns shipped change history
rules.summary: CHANGELOG should not become active work state, debugging history, or a handoff.

rules.title: Repository-wide handoff state must be bounded
rules.summary: A permanent root HANDOFF.md is a growth smell unless its responsibility and retirement boundary are explicit.

rules.title: Generic notes and logs need bounded ownership
rules.summary: Generic NOTES.md and LOG.md files should not act as unbounded sinks for unrelated lifecycles.

rules.title: Track alignment; latest released upstream is the target
rules.summary: Projects record the upstream source and last-aligned version, periodically compare with the latest released standard, and deliberately align rather than silently applying changes.

rules.title: Audit claims state coverage and evidence limits
rules.summary: Repository audits state what was inspected, what was unavailable or omitted, and do not convert missing evidence into a pass or defect.

rules.title: Exceptions are explicit and reviewable
rules.summary: Exceptions reference known rule IDs and include a reason; optional review dates surface stale exceptions.
